newsitem.title: USA: Gillette has record Q3, but European sales lag.
newsitem.headline: Gillette has record Q3, but European sales lag.

text.p: The Gillette Co on Thursday, while reporting the highest net income per common share for any quarter in the personal grooming giant's history, said weak European economies were cutting its market share there.

"Our combined European business experienced little topline growth in the third quarter. It was up about .04 percent and that's inclusive of unfavorable exchange rates," said Everett Howe, Gillette vice president for corporate investor relations in a conference call with analysts.
"Consumption is weak in France, Germany, Italy and Spain," said Howe.
An increase in unemployment in France, Germany and Italy "obviously has impacted our European business," Howe said.
Later in the call, he noted that, in weaker economies, "private labels tend to gain in popularity."

Nonetheless, Howe said the acquisition of the Czech blade maker Astra announced on Wednesday and an earlier acquisition of a Russian blade maker meant that Gillette had a "50 plus" share of the blade market worldwide.
The maker of deodorants, shaving creams, shampoos and aftershaves reported that toiletries had record third quarter profits of 110 percent.
Its third quarter earnings per share of 54 cents was one cent higher than the First Call consensus of 15 analysts.
"It represents the highest quarterly earnings per common share in the company's history," Howe said.
